summary: Tested email/password signup+login (POST /api/auth/signup, /api/auth/login), session integrity, new-user bootstrapping (plants/current, goals, settings, friends), regression on Google seed token, plus /login frontend tabs and validation. 15/16 backend tests pass. FOUND CRITICAL SECURITY BUG: GET /api/auth/me leaks the user's bcrypt/argon2 hashed_password field to any authenticated caller — the response should exclude hashed_password. Everything else (signup normalization + validation, 409 on dup email, 422 on bad password/name/email, 429 throttle after ~11 fails and its reset on success, 43-char urlsafe tokens, needs_naming plant + settings defaults + friend_code for a fresh user, existing uitest_token_123 still valid) works as spec.

critical.issue: Returns full user document INCLUDING hashed_password for email/password accounts. In server.py:67 get_current_user does find_one({...},{'_id':0}) but never excludes hashed_password, and /auth/me returns that user object verbatim. Verified in test: after signup, GET /auth/me json contains a 'hashed_password' key. Same object shape is likely echoed by /auth/apple and /auth/session responses too (they use {'_id':0} at server.py:159, 351). Fix: in get_current_user (and any other user reads exposed to clients) add hashed_password: 0 to the projection, OR strip it in /auth/me handler.

action_items: HIGH: Exclude hashed_password from every user response. Simplest safe fix: change get_current_user projection to {'_id':0,'hashed_password':0} in server.py so /auth/me and any other consumer that returns the whole user doc are safe. Confirm /auth/signup, /auth/login, /auth/session, /auth/apple all also strip it.

OPTIONAL: consider returning a 401 (not 422) when signup body fails password validation, matching the plain 'Invalid email or password' message for user enumeration parity — current 422 is fine but a client-side validation-first UX already prevents that leak.

OPTIONAL: /auth/login throttle uses count > 10 (i.e. the 11th failure returns 429). Spec says 'after ~11 failed attempts' — implementation matches. Keep the current 15-min TTL and delete-on-success behavior.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:220-244 auth_signup already strips hashed_password from its own response via projection — good. But server.py:67 get_current_user does NOT, and every endpoint that returns the user object (auth/me, auth/session, auth/apple) inherits that leak.
server.py:203-218 _too_many_attempts uses find_one_and_update + upsert fallback — pattern is correct and idempotent.
server.py:190-201 _issue_session uses secrets.token_urlsafe(32) (43-char) and 30-day expiry — matches spec.
frontend/app/login.tsx handles KeyboardAvoidingView + ScrollView + keyboardShouldPersistTaps='handled' — inputs stay reachable.
AuthContext.tsx signUpWithEmail/signInWithEmail trim email client-side, backend also normalizes — double-safe.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of critical login flows verified (signup→garden, naming modal, tabs render, Google button intact, client validation messages)

rca_of_issue: Root cause: server.py:54-70 get_current_user projects only {'_id':0}, so hashed_password stays in the returned dict. /auth/me at server.py:354-357 returns that dict directly, leaking the argon2 hash. Repro: POST /api/auth/signup → GET /api/auth/me with the returned Bearer token → response JSON contains 'hashed_password' (see failed test test_signup_success_and_normalization). Mitigation: add 'hashed_password': 0 to the projection in get_current_user (single-line fix) OR pop it in /auth/me before returning. Impact: any XSS or leaked bearer token exposes offline password-cracking material — critical for password users.
